thread.title: Football Preview: Can Patrick Henry climb back up to the region mountaintop?
thread.title_full: Football Preview: Can Patrick Henry climb back up to the region mountaintop?

author: Robby Fletcher Sports Editor
title: Football Preview: Can Patrick Henry climb back up to the region mountaintop?
text:
The Patrick Henry Patriots have seen some marvelous highs under the care of head coach Ken Wakefield, who’s entering his seventh season leading the program.
In his first season with Patrick Henry in 2019, the Patriots claimed the Region 4B title with a 10-4 record, and they nearly repeated as champs the following year with a 10-3 record and a 16-14 region finals loss to Varina.
The last two seasons have not seen those same highs from the program, however. They’re 4-16 in their last two campaigns, though not for a lack of effort or talent on the field. Last season, the Patriots went 2-8, losing three games by five points or less.
Entering the 2025 season, Wakefield has praised this team as a smart group of kids who have worked hard in preparation for the schedule ahead.
At the center of the offense is Wakefield’s son, Cole, a 6-foot-1, 215-pound junior quarterback. Last year, the Patriots got some quality play out of quarterback and star track runner Devin Roose, who has since graduated up to college athletics and is running track at William & Mary.
Wakefield doesn’t have the same foot speed as Roose, but he’s still a threat to pick up yards on the ground. At the JV level, Wakefield was a bruising downhill runner that consistently lowered his shoulder to fall forward for additional yardage. Near the goal line, he was an extremely difficult player to stop on quarterback draws up the middle. He can also attack the secondary with a big arm and unique mechanics that spiral deep shots over the middle.
Wakefield also has the luxury of a solid offensive line protecting him, which is headlined by 315-pound tackle Tristen Aguilar. The line also features three juniors in center Chance Smith, tackle Luke Patterson and guard Jackson Crowder. Sophomore Steven Garnett rounds out the starting lineup at guard opposite Crowder.
At the skill spots, seniors Cole Saunders and Jaevion Poindexter are primed for significant opportunities in the run and pass game. Saunders, standing at 5-foot-11 and 190 pounds, will be the team’s primary running back, while the 5-foot-10 Poindexter will operate from the slot. Last year, the rushing attack was led by Avery Curtis, who has since transferred to Hermitage High School for his senior year.
Much like the offensive line, there are three juniors in the passing game that should feature heavily, with wideouts Gabriel Dudkin and Tucker Roland emerging high on the depth chart and tight end Foster Hunt listed as a starter that will contribute as a pass-catcher and blocker.
The Patriots’ offense was shut out twice during a down season in 2024. They’ll look to their upperclassmen starters to step up and make sure that doesn’t happen this time around.
On defense, coach Wakefield’s base 3-4 system has a strong linebacking group that features Saunders, Poindexter, Hunt and junior Daniel Bird. There’s speed and ranginess out of that group, and they’ll look to get help attacking the backfield from a defensive line that features senior Justin Brooks and junior nose guard Josh Seay.
In the secondary, a pair of seniors in cornerback Malichi Mines and safety Aiden Gilbert will start in the back along with two juniors in cornerback Aidenn Hanks and safety Edwin Gonzalez.
The region has its share of stiff competition for Patrick Henry to take on, but the Patriots have high-level athletes and a proven and trusted coach to make them a team worth watching in 2025. They’ll open up their season on the road against the Bethel Bruins on Friday, Aug. 29. They’ll be at home a week later when they host the Godwin Eagles on Sept. 5.
